pr_body:
# Description

We implemented support for IAsyncDisposable within Blazor but we missed calling `DisposeAsync` when we tear down the renderer. (We only did the right thing when a component was removed while the app was running).

# Customer Impact
* Resources will not be properly cleaned when a circuit or Blazor webassembly app is terminated.

# Regression?

No. This feature was introduced in 5.0.

# Risk

Low. We are handling an additional case when we dispose the components.

## Fixes
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/26737

issue_context.title: IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync not called on Blazor component when tab is closed
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
A Blazor page can implement `IAsyncDisposable`. When navigating between pages, `DisposeAsync` gets called. However, when a browser tab is closed, `DisposeAsync` does not appear to be called.

If I implement `IDisposable` instead, `Dispose` gets properly called both when navigating away from the page, and closing the browser tab.

### To Reproduce
- Create a new Blazor server app
- Add a page `Index.razor`
- Add a code-behind file `Index.razor.cs` with the following content:

```csharp
public partial class Index : IAsyncDisposable
{
    [Inject]
    private ILogger<Index> Logger { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("Index page initialized.");
    }

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("Index page disposed.");
    }
}
```

- Set a breakpoint inside `DisposeAsync`
- Run the app, and navigate to the Index page. Close the tab and notice how the breakpoint isn't hit.

### Further technical details

review_comments: Does this mean `Dispose()` does not dispose these async components?
Dispose disposes async components, but doesn't wait for them to finish
We only call dispose async in our implementations, but I can't "remove" Dispose since is part of the public API
What do you feel about making a blocking call in `Dispose`? `Dispose() => DisposeAsync().AsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult()`? `DisposeAsync can call `Dispose(diposing: true)` directly
I'd rather remove it completely in a future release.
Can we use `_disposed` here to determine if this was previously invoked and no-op?
This was done, not sure why it doesn't show
